14-163.r: Child labour in hazardous work banned by all: Article 24 (no child under fourteen), UN Charter (childhood needs special assistance), and Supreme Court judgment of December 10, 1996.

14-164.r: Sir Ernest Barker: 'Rights without duties are like men without shadows'.

14-165.r: In India, rights and duties are correlative (two faces of the same thing); Holland: every right implies forbearance (a duty) by others.

14-166.r: Rights are claims of citizens against the State; they restrict State power and guard against State action.

14-167.r: Right to Service Act, by Official Gazette dates: Punjab → Assam → Gujarat → Maharashtra.

14-168.r: 'Right to Service' (time-bound delivery of public services) originated in Great Britain; India's 2011 Bill on time-bound delivery and grievance redressal was not passed.

14-169.r: Citizen's Charter aims: quality, time-bound service delivery, citizen-friendly and accountable governance; creating a hearing system for public demands is not its aim.

15-001.r: Purpose of Directive Principles → establish social and economic democracy, helping India grow as a welfare State.
hi: Directive Principles of State Policy (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व)

15-002.r: DPSP (Articles 36 to 51) aim at a welfare, secular, democratic State with socio-economic justice; not a religious State.

15-003.r: Both true, R explains A: DPSP aim at economic and social democracy; Article 38(1) → social order with social, economic, political justice; Article 37 → not court-enforceable.

15-004.r: DPSP are non-justiciable (cannot be enforced in any court); Fundamental Rights are enforceable.

15-005.r: Directive Principles are non-justiciable; Fundamental Rights are justiciable.

15-006.r: DPSP are instructions to Legislature and Executive on how to use their powers; they are not limitations on legislative or executive functions and are not court-enforceable.

15-007.r: Article 37: Part IV is not enforceable by any court, but is fundamental in governance; State must apply these principles in making laws.

15-008.r: Article 37 → Directive Principles (Part IV) are not enforceable by any court.

15-009.r: DPSP: not enforceable by courts, yet fundamental in governance; State's duty to apply them in making laws (both statements true).

15-010.r: DPSP spell out socio-economic democracy; not enforceable by any court; 'fundamental in the governance of the country'.

15-011.r: DPSP do not impose a legal duty on the State (non-enforceable, moral ideals), but are fundamental in governance and the State must apply them in law-making.

15-012.r: Welfare State concept → Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36 to 51).

15-015.r: Idea of India as a welfare State → found in both the Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy.

15-016.r: Constitution does not classify DPSP; by content they fall into three groups: Socialistic, Gandhian, Liberal-intellectual.

15-017.r: Directive Principles of State Policy → borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Ireland).
15-017.h: Directives from Dublin: DPSP came from Ireland.

15-020.r: Gandhian DPSP: village panchayats, rural cottage industries. Not Gandhian: Uniform Civil Code (liberal-intellectual), right to work (socialist).

15-021.r: Directive Principles are non-justiciable: not enforceable in any court of law in India.

15-022.r: Article 37 → Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, though not enforceable in courts.

15-023.r: Concentration of wealth violates DPSP: Article 39 directs equal right to livelihood for men and women and distribution of community's material resources for common good.

15-024.r: Equal pay for equal work for men and women → Article 39(d), a DPSP, not a Fundamental Right; SC read it with Articles 14, 16 (Randhir Singh, 1982).
15-024.t: Don't call it a Fundamental Right: the text is in DPSP; the Supreme Court only deduced it through Articles 14 and 16.

15-027.r: Panchayati Raj → DPSP, Article 40: State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

15-028.r: Article 40 → State organises village panchayats (a DPSP). Article 48 → ban cow slaughter; Article 33 → Parliament modifies Fundamental Rights for forces.
15-028.t: Article 33 is in Part III (Fundamental Rights), not a Directive Principle.

15-031.r: Village Panchayat → Article 40; Uniform Civil Code → 44; Agriculture and Animal Husbandry → 48; Separation of Judiciary → 50; International Peace → 51.

15-032.r: Article 40 → village panchayats; 41 → right to work, education, public assistance; 44 → Uniform Civil Code; 48 → agriculture and animal husbandry.

15-033.r: Wrong pair: Article 48 → organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, not separation of judiciary. Correct: 39A free legal aid; 40 village panchayats; 44 Uniform Civil Code.

15-034.r: Article 39(d) → equal pay for equal work for men and women. Others: free legal aid 39A; agriculture and animal husbandry 48; village panchayat 40.

15-035.r: Equal justice and free legal aid → Article 39A; Protection of environment → 48A; Right to Work → 41; Protection of monuments → 49.

15-036.r: Wrong pair: co-operative societies → Article 43B, not 43A; Article 43A → workers' participation in management. Article 50 separation of judiciary; 46 SC/ST interests; 40 panchayats.

15-037.r: MGNREGA → at least 100 days' employment a year to a rural household (A true); right to work is a DPSP, not in Part III (R false).

15-038.r: MGNREGA implements Article 43 (DPSP): State to secure a living wage, decent working conditions and leisure for all workers.

15-039.r: Article 43A (workers' participation in management of industries) → inserted by the 42nd Amendment. Uniform Civil Code → Article 44.

15-042.r: Separation of judiciary from executive → Article 50, a Directive Principle (Part IV).

15-043.r: Article 51 → promotion of international peace and security. 41 → right to work, education, public assistance; 43A → workers in management; 48A → environment, forests, wildlife.

15-044.r: International peace and security → DPSP, Article 51 (linked to foreign policy): just and honourable relations, respect for international law, settle disputes by arbitration.

15-047.r: Added by 42nd Amendment: 39(f) protection of children and youth, 39A free legal aid, 43A workers' participation. Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) was not added by it.

15-049.r: Constitution grants the right against exploitation to children, women and tribals; the word 'Dalit' is not in the Constitution.

15-050.r: Free education for children up to 14 (old Article 45) is no longer a DPSP (changed 2002). DPSPs: prohibition of intoxicating drinks (47), cow protection (48), environment (48A).

15-052.r: Prohibition of intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs (except medicinal) → DPSP, Article 47; ban on trafficking and forced labour → Fundamental Right, Article 23(1).

15-053.r: Gandhian DPSPs: village panchayats (Article 40), rural cottage industries, nutrition and public health (47), cow protection (48). Uniform Civil Code and workers' leisure are not Gandhian.

15-054.r: Environment, forests and wildlife → both DPSP (Article 48A) and Fundamental Duty (Article 51A(g)).
15-054.h: State protects (48A), citizen protects (51A g); g for green.

15-055.r: Protection of environment → part of both DPSP (Article 48A, State's duty) and Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A(g), citizen's duty).

15-056.r: 'State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment' → DPSP, Article 48A. Equality before law and non-discrimination are Fundamental Rights.

15-057.r: DPSP are silent on adult education. Included: living wage (Article 43), free legal aid (39A), early childhood care and education below six (45).

15-058.r: Free legal aid (Article 39A) → added later by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976; panchayats, cow slaughter ban and Uniform Civil Code were not later additions.

15-059.r: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid) → inserted by 42nd Amendment Act 1976 (in force 3 January 1977).
